summary: You present a strong, coherent ZYZZsat mission design: all required elements are addressed, STK evidence and hand calculations support the orbital, coverage, data-budget and decay work, and the report is well structured. The main gaps are the absent full X-band link budget and the assumed Mount Pleasant ground-station fit-out; launch dispersion and revisit claims are minor uncertainties.
next_steps: Add a complete X-band link budget in Section 2.4 (EIRP, G/T, path loss, modulation/coding, Eb/N0 margin) and substantiate whether the Mount Pleasant 12 m antenna can support the assumed S/X-band fit-out, or propose a verified alternative.
Replace the fixed 60% usable-contact-time assumption in Table 6 with elevation-dependent pass modelling and scheduling, and use it to quantify realistic data throughput and latency.

Strengthen the launch and revisit arguments: justify Vega C/rideshare injection dispersion to 600 km and 97.79° without propulsion, and support the 'any reef within five days' claim with latitude, daylight and cloud coverage analysis.

criteria.C1: In Section 1 you clearly state the primary mission, need, single-spacecraft rationale and AIMS operator/customers, with an Australia focus and references. To secure full marks within Accomplished, strengthen the evidence base with more scholarly/peer-reviewed sources and explicitly link each rationale point to a design requirement or performance driver.
criteria.C2: Sections 2.2–2.5 give a comprehensive design with STK screenshots/files and sound orbital and decay checks. For full marks, add a complete X-band link budget, substantiate the Mount Pleasant S/X-band fit-out, replace the fixed 60% contact-time assumption in Table 6 with elevation-dependent pass scheduling, and address Vega C/rideshare dispersion and the 'any reef within five days' revisit claim more rigorously.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion follows the evidence, summarises key performance values and identifies four limitations. To reach full marks, link each limitation explicitly to the affected design decision or requirement and quantify its impact where possible, so the reader can see priorities for future work.
criteria.C4: The report has a clear engineering structure, a concise executive summary, labelled figures/tables and citations that match the bibliography. For full marks, polish the remaining presentation/reference-quality issues—ensure all sources are appropriate and formatting is fully consistent throughout—so the document reads at a professional standard.
